mostWorthwhile.text: Making shells and burying them in sediment was the most worthwhile passage: the physical inference led to fossils, while the explanation made clear how incomplete the fossil record is.

leastWorthwhile.text: The opening inspections felt somewhat repetitive: each of the first two revealed just one partner and immediately combined it, although they did move the chapter forward.

surprise.text: The algae branch completed its goal but also revealed a new goal about preserving traces of life, expanding the chapter beyond the two original objectives.

arbitrary.text: Water turning partnered cells into colonies felt more like a mythic gesture than a clearly explained mechanism; the later account of cellular cooperation helped, but did not explain that particular combination.

continue.text: Yes. The branching animal and algae paths, the fossil detour, and the careful qualifications about evolution make me curious how the living world develops next.
